# Marketing skills for Claude

These are the marketing skills I give away in my free course, AI Fluency for Ambitious Marketers. Each one turns Claude into someone who does a real marketing job properly: a copywriter who writes like your brand and proves what it says, an analyst who reads campaign numbers without being fooled by them, a reviewer who argues against your plan before your CFO does.

I'm Paul Dervan. I run Run with Foxes, where we build AI agents for marketing teams, and I teach marketing at UCD. I was Ireland's Marketer of the Year in 2022. Everything here is used in the course, and the course shows each skill working, step by step: [runwithfoxes.com/course](https://runwithfoxes.com/course). It's free.

## The skills

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [ai-writer](../skills/ai-writer) | Writes emails, blog posts and web pages from your brand's own positioning, messaging and tone of voice. Shows you its plan first, then audits its draft for slop and unproven claims and scores itself honestly. |
| [brand-interviewer](../skills/brand-interviewer) | Interviews you one question at a time and hands back a finished brand document: audience, competitors, proof, positioning, tone of voice, messaging framework. The writer reads these. |
| [red-team](../skills/red-team) | Attacks a document or an AI answer to find what will not survive a sharp reader: unsupported claims, hidden assumptions, weak logic, buried risk. |
| [cfo-review](../skills/cfo-review) | Reads your business case the way a sceptical CFO would and gives a plain verdict, and what would turn a no into a yes. |
| [campaign-analyst](../skills/campaign-analyst) | Reads campaign and channel data with ten rules that stop the usual mistakes, starting with platforms marking their own homework. |
| [segmentation-check](../skills/segmentation-check) | Tests whether a group of customers someone calls a segment really is one, against your customer file, before it gets its own playbook and budget. |
| [segmentation-audit](../skills/segmentation-audit) | Audits a whole segmentation study in seven stages, using Wiemer Snijders' method, to find the few differences that are real. |
| [market-research](../skills/market-research) | Desk research on what a market is actually saying, with ten rules that make it harder to fool. |
| [website-builder](../skills/website-builder) | The order of work for a marketer building a website that does not look like everyone else's. |
| [web-design-expert](../skills/web-design-expert) | Your web designer: layout, type, colour, page order, forms, mobile, speed, and building with Next.js and Vercel. |
| [klaviyo-expert](../skills/klaviyo-expert) | Answers Klaviyo and lifecycle email questions from a checked knowledge pack. |
| [learn-a-subject](../skills/learn-a-subject) | How the two expert packs above were made. Use it to make Claude your expert on any tool. |

There is a worked example in [examples/kite](../examples/kite): Kite Insurance, a made-up insurer, with its brand documents, a year of campaign data, 4,000 customers and its market research. The course uses it for practice, and so can you.

## How to use them

In Claude Code, copy a skill's folder into `.claude/skills/` in your project, or into `~/.claude/skills/` to have it everywhere. Then ask for the job in plain words, "help me create my audience document" or "red team this plan", and Claude picks the right skill.

In the Claude app, zip a skill's folder and upload it under Settings, Capabilities, Skills. Or start a Project and add the files to it, which is how the course does it.

The writer works best once the brand interviewer has made your brand documents. Start with your audience document. The rest lean on it.

## A few things worth knowing

These skills don't know your business. The writer can't invent your positioning and the analyst can't invent your numbers, and both will tell you so rather than guess. What they bring is the method. You bring what you know.

They are mine, and they reflect how I work, which is quality first, then automate what repeats. Some files date from autumn 2026 and say so. Tools like Klaviyo change often, so check anything where a date or a price matters.

If you use them in your own work, I'd like to hear how it goes. You'll find me at [runwithfoxes.com](https://runwithfoxes.com).
